en_summary: Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla would probably be better together, but a merger needs shareholder votes and he can’t drag SpaceX holders into a bad deal without getting sued.
text:
Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla would probably be better together, but a merger needs shareholder votes and he can’t drag SpaceX holders into a bad deal without getting sued

“You don’t need them to be together, but would they be better together? I mean, probably, yes. This is not like, let’s merge the companies no matter what. These require shareholder votes, which may or may not succeed, at least in the case of Tesla.”

“But even for my shareholder vote for SpaceX, I have to represent other shareholders. I can’t just drag them into a non-economic merger that is bad for them, because I’ll obviously get sued.”

“So it really is just a question of, do SpaceX and Tesla execute better together and create more value than if they’re apart? Does that hypothesis stand up to scrutiny? And that will be up to the shareholders to decide. But there are so many areas of convergence that didn’t exist in years before, and are increasingly significant to the future.”

Its AI models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL, delivering roughly a year's worth of chip-design progress in less than 5 months, with some changes moving into production. AMD verified single-digit PPA improvements on upcoming CPU blocks, and OpenAI's Jalapeño chip saw 13% and 10% area reductions verified on silicon. OpenAI is also developing GPT-Synopsys with Synopsys.
text:
OPENAI REPORTS UP TO 14% PPA IMPROVEMENT ON $AMD GPU DESIGNS

OpenAI says its AI models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL for AMD's already heavily optimized flagship GPU IP, delivering roughly a year's worth of chip-design progress in less than 5 months.

The improvements involve power, performance and area (PPA), with several results already moving into production:

GPU: Up to 14% PPA improvement on flagship GPU IP.

Manufacturing: AMD has incorporated some AI-generated changes into a recent chip design sent for manufacturing, with others added to production design files for future versions.

CPU: AMD verified single-digit PPA improvements across key blocks of its upcoming next-generation flagship CPU.

OpenAI's Jalapeño chip: AI-assisted optimizations reduced standard-cell area by approximately 13% in its vector unit and 10% in its matrix unit, with the improvements verified on silicon.

OpenAI is also working with Synopsys to develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model designed to use professional chip-design and verification tools.

MICROSOFT TO USE $INTC'S EMIB PACKAGING FOR AZURE CHIPS

$MSFT is the FIRST company to announce plans to use Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging for its own Azure silicon. 

EMIB connects multiple chiplets within a single package, allowing more flexible chip designs.

The new long-term agreement with Intel also secures multi-year Xeon CPU supply for Azure, including next-gen Diamond Rapids processors.

The companies will also expand work on CXL memory, Intel QuickAssist acceleration and TDX confidential computing, including encryption of VM memory and CPU state during host migrations.

Intel says its existing Azure optimizations deliver:

- Up to 2.3x greater performance and memory flexibility in Azure M-series v4 VMs using Xeon 6 and CXL memory.

- Up to 2.5x faster SQL backups through QuickAssist-enabled Azure VMs.

✅They didn’t file their 10q at the same time as earnings release as was their custom. Red Flag 🚩 

✅The call and Q&A didn’t address investor concerns. They claimed zero sales to China. That is laughable. 

✅After call very large holders of stock get to talk to management. They ask tougher questions than sell side. Collectively they likely didn’t like the answers or legal speak non answers. In short they don’t believe the future guidance is real. The pop in the morning was sold and continues as of this post. This is called a long squeeze…opposite of short squeeze. 

Bottom line: The market is worried that the former CFO and Board are in CYA mode on the China question and reported Jensen’s numbers and guidance but didn’t file 10q and sign off on them legally yet. Speculation is that they will open the kimono on China numbers after an investigation and pretend they didn’t know. 

Additionally the other problems for the stock are: 

-competition will take advantage of leadership disruption and gross margins will eventually go lower. 
-Neo clouds are having trouble getting financing to buy more chips. 
-The DSOs of receivables went to 64 from 60 last Q and 45 prior. Customers are taking longer to pay essentially. 
-SEC investigation and DOJ investigation overhang
-And finally macro concerns that the credit markets are questioning the build out of AI and the cycle

$Tencent / Chinese CSPs’ tone on the AI capex cycle is very clear - 

Martin Lau laid out a clear case for why AI capex should moderate after 2027:

1/ Front-loaded investment: AI infrastructure is like building a factory. Once built, it can continuously train new models and generate tokens.

2/ Lower hardware costs: The same equipment should cost significantly less by 2028.

3/ Rapid efficiency gains: The same infrastructure can deliver exponentially more training compute and token output over time.

Takeaway: Martin is effectively calling for a peak in AI capex in 2026-27, with a meaningful decline in capex intensity thereafter, even as AI demand continues to grow.

The read-through for semis is interesting: If annual industry AI capex eventually normalizes below $1T, assigning a mid-range multiple to normalized earnings, that’s your industry total size.

Highlights true moat in top-tier tech roadmap and engineering, Rubin first quarter $20B orders confirmed with 1 month deployment efficiency double previous and 10x token/watt vs Blackwell, implying 1GW Rubin revenue $40-50B per year. System engineering with own CPU/connect/security chips and CPO next year. Diversified revenue beyond cloud, supporting neoclouds, enterprises, sovereign. Refutes off-balance sheet concerns: $640B commitments mostly supply chain locks for wafers/HBM/packaging, $100B own cloud, $32B neocloud with conditions, OpenAI 20-year exclusive. Despite Huang exit short-term impact, fundamentals strong, valuation premium needs adjustment to long-term reasonable, event-driven buy points.
text:
$NVDA 最新Q3财报财务数据和下一季预测全面超预期，粉碎的是空头的“半导体算力周期见顶和估值塌陷”的小作文陷阱。  

一个人能活成黄仁勋这种离职能带崩2万亿自己创业公司市值，还能带崩整个AI泡沫，那真是可以笑傲江湖了。如何真正的解读背后事件以及财报中关键的英伟达投资策略“范式”转移？

真正的行业专家背景买方投资看的当然不只是一个收入和毛利超预期，这都是大概率。要看到这种英伟达顶级的技术路线和工程实现能力，这才是真正的护城河

8月启动发售新一代Rubin第一个季度就200亿订单确认，部署效率1个月比上一代快一倍，而且新一代的token/瓦的效率是上一代Blackwell的十倍提升，意味着1GW的Rubin收入就是一年4-500亿。

这不是简单卖GPU，而是真正的系统工程，自己的CPU/连接/安全芯片/明年上光互连CPO量产又一能效提升。加上模块化工厂，按上接点就挣钱。这个背景就是大的行业需求暴涨，特别是Agentic AI对于算力需求，哪怕老卡早期前2代的租金都在大涨。

收入多元化除了云大厂占1半，这也是为什么英伟达要扶持第三方新云公司，包括企业/主权等收入，降低依赖于单一大客户风险，何况中国收入为0，目前北美/欧日等需求直接填补空档，供不应求。

哪怕是市场担心的表外担保生态融资，来虚增收入，完全可以证伪。6400亿表外承诺，近4000亿是供应链采购承诺主要是锁定上游晶圆/HBM存储和封装产能，这是必须的，因为英伟达自己是轻资产，对于上游的供应链掌控重要性。当然老黄不在有短期影响，但对于英伟达这种体量客户，靠个人关系已经不是长久之计，必然规范大势所趋，这方面何况作为最大的客户，英伟达是甲方，不担心台湾供应链不保障的风险

另外1000亿是自用云服务；真正新云neocloud保底租赁也就是320亿，而且都是有明确前置条件，就是全部上线才担保，现在供不应求之下，风险何在？另外1000多亿是OpenAI的20年独家租约，至少目前看不到证伪。

目前市场大跌因为黄仁勋的时代落幕，当然作为创始人的远见和个人魄力是有折价，这主要体现在可能未来3-5年战略的选择，但是对于AI时代真正的王者和领头羊，老黄一人独裁的邪修管理风格，也是必然在企业进入系统化竞争的平台后，管理范式的转移，向“开宗立派”转移，只不过，他个人事件离职，加速了这个转移而已。

从投资策略和估值角度，事件性冲击短期当然是重点，根据不同的事件会有好的买入时点，结合合理的估值，因为基本面虽然强，但是整体的估值溢价需要下调到一个中长期合理的区间，同时也要考虑本质性，一些竞争力丧失的风险，比如法律和治理风险，人才流失风险。

颗粒度更细的投资策略和估值，见订阅者专享。教育分享。
